chapter: Armstrong, Big Sid and Joe Glaser
title: Louis Armstrong's generosity and Stuff Crouch's club
summary: Louis gave money to everyone, including Stuff Crouch, whom he set up with an after-hours club and a big Chrysler, and Crouch charged the band when they came over; Louis paid for Crouch's funeral.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: Louie was a very generous person.

Oh, yes. Some (Unintelligible) musicians used to take him, like, for a fool. They thought he was a fool. But he used to tell me, he said, "Pops," he said, "them characters think I don't know," he said, "but I just give them poor so and so a few dollars."
Money didn't bother him. That's funny. And he had women strung all over the world, put them in business, even. He had one guy that used to live here called Stuff Crouch, Crotch, Crouch?
Stuff Crouch, Julius Crouch, yes, uh-huh.
He put him in business, gave him an after-hour place.

So he came over there at Billy Berg's, after the place opened up. He invited the group over to the place for some drinks and a little snack if they wanted. Now, Louie put him in that business, now. And by a quirk, I didn't go, I didn't feel like going. It was something -- I didn't go. And the guys that went, Earl Hines and [Jack Teagarden] all the rest of them, went over there. And when they were getting ready to leave, Crouch gave them a check. And that burned Louie up. And he used to send his kid, like, go to Billy Berg's -- he'd send his kid to talk to Louie, like, telling Louie he's her uncle and all that business.
Yeah, well, he was the godfather to one of his daughters, --
-- and his daughters -- Julie and -- I can't think of the other girl's name -- Cheryl, Julie and
Cheryl. And then he had a son, Howard, who sang under the name of Dave Howard, and Louie helped him, too.
Helped him to get a record. Then when Stuff died, Louie paid for the funeral.
He helps everybody. The man, he -- money doesn't mean nothing to him.
